newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Moody's may downgrade Dresdner Bank.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Moody's may downgrade Dresdner Bank.

text.p: Top rated German banking giant Dresdner Bank AG may be downgraded by Moody's Investors Service because of the toll taken by intense competitive pressures, the rating agency said on Friday.

Moody's placed Dresdner's long-term senior Aaa ratings and its A bank financial strength ratings under review for possible downgrade. The agency also said it might downgrade Dresdner subsidiaries Kleinwort Benson Group Plc, Dresdner Bank Luxembourg S.A. and Banque Internationale de Placement.
Tighter competition, narrower lending yields, flatter loan demand, and rising funding costs had led to a decline in Dresdner's traditional revenue sources.

"The review will also consider the potential new risks that have been introduced through Dresdner's focused growth strategy in asset management and certain trading and investment banking businesses," the agency said in a statement.

Moody's noted that Dresdner was characterised by a solid universal banking franchise, good asset quality and stable earnings which were likely to keep it among the financially sounder banks worldwide.

"However, the bank's high cost structure, its more modest core capitalisation and the rising scale of global competition are factors that may no longer be consistent with the highest ratings," Moody's said.
Moody's confirmed the Prime-1 ratings for short-term deposits and commercial paper for Dresdner and its rated subsidiaries.
Dresdner Bank is the second largest private sector bank in Germany with group assets at September 30, 1996 of 541 billion marks ($338 billion), Moody's said.
